page.layout: One page of text, with the running head and page number at the top. The centred italic line "Quid est Additio?" sits under the running head as a heading. Below it is one column of running text with the italic centred heading "Exemplum." and a short worked sum at the end. No marginal notes, no footnotes.

main_text.l: Est numeratio, qua numerus addicur numero,
Sub numeris addedis lineam rectam tra-
hito, & à dextra versus sinistram sursum co-
jungito omnes notas primas: quod si ex ta-
li additione digitus emerserit, is infra linea
directe sub primis figuris est scribendus: si
dextram notam pone, altera mente servata,
Iunctis autem primis, eodem modo se-
cundas collige, quibus expeditis, ad tertias
Cùm verò ad ultimum locum deveneris,
Et sic dico: unum & 4 sunt 5, quae directè
sunt 3, quae subnoto. Inductio sic est:

page.notes: The "1 1 1" carry-over marks and the small digits above the second row are printed as a sum layout; the first row is copied as printed. "habetur[?]": the r is damaged on the scan. Long s has been written as plain s throughout, per the rules. "addicur" is printed so; it may be a printing error for "adiicitur", left as printed.
